messages.subject: Individual ID# versus (R/qtl's intrinsic) "index" #
parts:
Karl:  

I realize that I can use the R/qtl getid(cross) command to get a complete listing of my own assigned ID# for individuals in my cross (when I have included that ID# as the first "phenotype" in the *.csv file).  

However, this command is not really useful in those situations where I am only interested in a subset of "index" numbers that R/qtl intrinsically assigns to individuals in a cross object, WHEN my own assigned ID# for those individuals is not also an ordered contiguous set of consecutive true numbers (or worse, the ID# is alphanumeric text).  

If I want to pull out a vector of (intrinsic) "index" numbers and determine my correspondent ID#s (and vice versa), how would I go about doing that?  

A command for doing the foregoing  would be quite helpful when examining portions of R/qtl generated plots or tables that display the individual index # on an axis or in a column or row.  R/qtls cmds exist, of course, for doing this with marker index numbers.  

Sorry to bother you with my question, but I looked at the R/qtl command manual and could not find (or else simply overlooked) an obvious method for addressing this issue..  

Any suggestions?

- Jim

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Individual ID# versus (R/qtl's intrinsic) "index" #
parts:
I only vaguely understand what you're seeking. If I've guessed correctly, the match() function may be sufficient for you.

# load hyper data
data(hyper)
# create a bunch of random IDs
hyper$pheno$id <- paste("mouse", sample(1000:9999, nind(hyper)), sep="")

# sample 25 ids at random, as some subset of interest
someids <- sample(hyper$pheno$id, 25)

# use match to identify the numeric index within the cross to which these correspond
match(someids, getid(hyper))
[1] 104 149 136 189 87 69 242 75 215 100 78 33 94 29 218 62 38 122 116 180 96 129 28 42 210


karl
